text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.
* Prime minister Romano Prodi met interior minister Giorgio Napolitano in order to discuss immigration (all).

* Separatist Northern League leader Umberto Bossi accused Pope John Paul II of meddling in politics and misguiding the Roman Catholic Church. Bossi pointed out he did not mean to blame the Pope as much as the Roman Catholic Church itself (all).

* Prime Minister Romano Prodi says he agrees with German Chancellor Helmut Kohl that euro currency must be stable, and reiterates that Italy must reach a deficit/GDP ratio of 3.0 percent, not 3.1 or 3.2 percent.

* Retail chain Standa, a unit of opposition leader Silvio Berliusconi's Fininvest holding, said it would launch a stock buyback from August 26 to September 19 as part of a restructuring plan (La Repubblica).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
